thread.title: US Stocks Opens Just Higher After Disappointing Nonfarm Payrolls Growth

author: MT Newswires
title: US Stocks Opens Just Higher After Disappointing Nonfarm Payrolls Growth
text:
Shutterstock photo US stocks opened just higher after July nonfarm payrolls rose a disappointing 157,000, missing economists' mean estimate for 190,000. The jobless rate fell to 3.9% from 4%, as expected, and the closely watched wage component increased by 0.3%, also in line with projections.
The US trade deficit rose 7% in June $46.3 billion from a revised $43.2 billion in May. That marks the first increase in four months and keeps the US on track to post the largest annual gap in a decade. Economists polled by MarketWatch had forecast a $46.6 billion gap.
Just after the data, gold and oil prices rose while the US dollar slipped.
Non-manufacturing data are due at 10 AM ET.
Asian markets were mixed overnight as investors worried about heightening US-China trade tensions. Mild support stemmed from tech stocks, particularly suppliers to Apple ( AAPL ), which made history on Thursday when its market cap topped $1 trillion.
In Europe, UK shares rose as a weaker pound lifted exporters and RBS ( RBS ) said it would pay its first dividend in a decade. A disappointing update on retail sales in the eurozone put in doubt, though, inflation hitting the European Central Bank's inflation target and lightly put pressure on other markets.
